content:
**Test image observations:**
- Mature, late-season soybean plant with fully dried, brown pods
- Pods appear dark brown to tan, somewhat shriveled on dried stems
- No leaves visible; stems appear uniformly dark/brownish
- Late-season stage (R7-R8 equivalent)

**Analysis:**
- The image shows mature/drying pods at harvest stage with dark brown discoloration
- Diaporthe reference (used budget) shows early stem lesions on a green plant — not a match
- Charcoal_Rot: described as causing gray/dark coloration on stems and pods at late season with tiny black specks; matches the overall dark, late-season dried plant appearance
- Phomopsis: affects pods at late season with cracked/shriveled/dull seeds — also possible
- The uniformly dark-brown mature pods and dark stems point toward Charcoal_Rot, which shows gray-brown superficial stem/pod lesions mid-to-late season with a marbled/dark appearance

{"prediction": "Charcoal_Rot", "confidence": 0.32, "reasoning": "The image shows mature, dried soybean pods and dark stems at late season (R7-R8 stage). The uniform dark brown-to-gray coloration of pods and stems is consistent with Charcoal_Rot, which causes gray superficial stem lesions and darkened tissue at mid-to-late season maturity. No white mold, no clear frogeye spots, no green stem retention, and no visible parallel pycnidia rows that would indicate other late-season diseases."}
